Threshold selection Training-only Youden’s J
Selected threshold 0.081
Specificity 67.2%

Key predictors used in the model:

  • Order value
  • Freight cost
  • Number of items
  • Number of sellers
  • Estimated delivery window
  • Maximum payment installments
  • Purchase month
  • Primary payment type

Skewed monetary variables were log-transformed before modeling.

Practical Interpretation
  • Accuracy near 67% is misleading under class imbalance.
  • Precision is only 15.3%; use as a screening tool, not an automatic decision rule.
  • Association does not prove causation. Log-transformed monetary odds ratios are not one-real changes.
Limitation

Late deliveries are imbalanced, precision remains low, and undelivered or canceled orders are excluded from the modeling sample.

Method, population, and class distribution

Delivered orders with valid estimated and actual delivery dates, complete predictors, and non-not_paid payment type.

Partition On-Time (0) Late (1)
Training 70,915 6,260
Test 17,729 1,565

Threshold 0.081 selected on training data using Youden’s J because class imbalance (late prevalence = 8.11%) made the default 0.50 threshold predict almost no late orders (training sensitivity = 0.001, F1 = 0.002 at 0.50).
